ln.intro.text: Storm's coming in, keeper. Let's light the way for every ship.
ln.intro.speaker: hoot

ln.back.text: Welcome back to the lamp room, keeper. The ships are waiting.
ln.back.speaker: hoot

ln.story.intro1.text: A storm rolls over Number Hill harbour. The wind howls, and the sea turns black.

ln.story.intro2.text: Hoot keeps the old lighthouse. Tonight, four ships are still out at sea.

ln.story.intro3.text: His lamp, his chart and his compass can bring them home, with careful maths.

ln.story.intro4.text: Will you keep watch with me? Let's guide every ship home.
ln.story.intro4.speaker: hoot

ln.story.between2.text: The first ship is turning for home. Steady work, keeper.
ln.story.between2.speaker: hoot

ln.story.between4.text: Halfway through the night. The storm is easing a little.

ln.story.between6.text: One more ship is still out there. Bobbo's little boat.
ln.story.between6.speaker: hoot

ln.story.outro1.text: One by one, the ships followed the beam through the rocks.

ln.story.outro2.text: Every ship is safe in harbour. Thank you, keeper.
ln.story.outro2.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.tutorial.text: The beam meets the straight harbour wall. Find the angle x, then press Done.
ln.prompt.tutorial.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.line.text: The harbour wall is a straight line. Find the missing angle.
ln.prompt.line.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.point.text: The beams shine out all the way round the lamp. Find the missing angle.
ln.prompt.point.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.kind.text: Follow the beam's sweep. What type of angle is it?
ln.prompt.kind.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.vert.text: Two straight beams cross at the lamp. Find the missing angle.
ln.prompt.vert.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.tri.text: The lighthouse, the buoy and the ship make a triangle. Find the missing angle.
ln.prompt.tri.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.iso.text: This triangle has two equal sides. Find the missing angle.
ln.prompt.iso.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.par.text: The two shipping lanes are parallel. Find the missing angle.
ln.prompt.par.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.reason.text: Which angle fact links the two marked angles?
ln.prompt.reason.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.bread.text: What's the bearing of the ship from the lighthouse? Use three figures.
ln.prompt.bread.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.bback.text: A ship can see our lamp, but we can't see the ship. Turn the beam towards it.
ln.prompt.bback.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.hyp.text: How long is the sloping side?
ln.prompt.hyp.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.leg.text: We know the longest side. Find the shorter one.
ln.prompt.leg.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.round.text: Find the length, to one decimal place.
ln.prompt.round.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.conv.text: Is the corner of my new bracket a right angle?
ln.prompt.conv.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.real.text: Use the chart's scale. How far is it really?
ln.prompt.real.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.map.text: How far apart are they on the chart?
ln.prompt.map.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.share.text: Share the supplies in the ratio on the card.
ln.prompt.share.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.ratio.text: Write the chart's scale as a ratio, one to n.
ln.prompt.ratio.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.plot.text: Drop the marker buoy at the coordinates on the card.
ln.prompt.plot.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.grad.text: What's the gradient of this ship's path?
ln.prompt.grad.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.icpt.text: Where does this path cross the y-axis?
ln.prompt.icpt.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.eqn.text: Which equation matches this ship's path?
ln.prompt.eqn.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.meet.text: Two ships, two straight paths. Where do they cross?
ln.prompt.meet.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.para.text: Which ship's path will never cross the Gull's?
ln.prompt.para.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.fline.text: Bobbo's boat is the last one out. Find the angle to light his way.
ln.prompt.fline.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.ftri.text: Bobbo's boat is the last one out. Find the angle at his boat.
ln.prompt.ftri.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.fback.text: Bobbo can see our lamp. Turn the beam to his boat.
ln.prompt.fback.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.fchart.text: How far is Bobbo's boat from the harbour, in a straight line?
ln.prompt.fchart.speaker: hoot

ln.prompt.fcourse.text: Which straight course brings Bobbo's boat into the harbour?
ln.prompt.fcourse.speaker: hoot

ln.help.line.text: A straight line is half a turn. The angles along it add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
ln.help.line.speaker: ripple

ln.help.point.text: All the way round a point is a full turn: three hundred and sixty degrees.
ln.help.point.speaker: ripple

ln.help.kind.text: Compare the sweep with a right angle, then with a straight line.
ln.help.kind.speaker: ripple

ln.help.vert.text: Where two straight lines cross, the opposite angles are equal.
ln.help.vert.speaker: ripple

ln.help.tri.text: The three angles inside any triangle add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
ln.help.tri.speaker: ripple

ln.help.iso.text: Two equal sides mean two equal angles, at the ends of the third side.
ln.help.iso.speaker: ripple

ln.help.par.text: Look for the letter shape: F angles are equal, Z angles are equal, C angles add to one eighty.
ln.help.par.speaker: ripple

ln.help.reason.text: Trace the lines between the two angles. Do they make an F, a Z or a C?
ln.help.reason.speaker: ripple

ln.help.bread.text: Bearings start at north and turn clockwise. Always write three figures.
ln.help.bread.speaker: ripple

ln.help.bback.text: If the ship sees us one way, we see the ship the opposite way: half a turn round.
ln.help.bback.speaker: ripple

ln.help.hyp.text: Square the two shorter sides, add them, then take the square root.
ln.help.hyp.speaker: ripple

ln.help.leg.text: Start from the longest side squared, and take away the other side squared.
ln.help.leg.speaker: ripple

ln.help.round.text: Work it out exactly first, then round to one decimal place.
ln.help.round.speaker: ripple

ln.help.conv.text: Square all three sides. If the two small squares add up to the big one, it's a right angle.
ln.help.conv.speaker: ripple

ln.help.real.text: Every centimetre on the chart stands for the same distance at sea.
ln.help.real.speaker: ripple

ln.help.map.text: Work backwards: how many lots of the scale fit into the real distance?
ln.help.map.speaker: ripple

ln.help.share.text: Add the ratio numbers to find how many equal parts there are.
ln.help.share.speaker: ripple

ln.help.ratio.text: A ratio needs the same units on both sides. Turn the kilometres into centimetres.
ln.help.ratio.speaker: ripple

ln.help.plot.text: Coordinates go across first, then up. Along the corridor, then up the stairs.
ln.help.plot.speaker: ripple

ln.help.grad.text: Gradient is rise divided by run. Read from left to right.
ln.help.grad.speaker: ripple

ln.help.icpt.text: The y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis, where x is zero.
ln.help.icpt.speaker: ripple

ln.help.eqn.text: In y equals m x plus c, m is the gradient and c is where it crosses the y-axis.
ln.help.eqn.speaker: ripple

ln.help.meet.text: Where two paths cross, the point fits both equations.
ln.help.meet.speaker: ripple

ln.help.para.text: Parallel paths have the same gradient, so they never meet.
ln.help.para.speaker: ripple

ln.help.fline.text: Use the straight line first. Then share what's left between the two equal angles.
ln.help.fline.speaker: ripple

ln.help.ftri.text: Two steps: the straight line gives you one inside angle, then the triangle gives the last.
ln.help.ftri.speaker: ripple

ln.help.fback.text: Bobbo sees us one way, so we see him the opposite way.
ln.help.fback.speaker: ripple

ln.help.fchart.text: East and north make a right angle. Pythagoras first, then the scale.
ln.help.fchart.speaker: ripple

ln.help.fcourse.text: Find the gradient from the two points, then where the line crosses the y-axis.
ln.help.fcourse.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.line360.text: Three sixty is a full turn. A straight line is only half a turn.
ln.hint.ang.line360.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.same.text: The two angles aren't equal. Together they make the straight line.
ln.hint.ang.same.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.complement.text: Ninety is a right angle. A straight line is twice that.
ln.hint.ang.complement.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.addOnly.text: Good start: you added the angles you know. Now take that from the whole amount.
ln.hint.ang.addOnly.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.point180.text: These beams go all the way round, not just along a line. That's a full turn.
ln.hint.ang.point180.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.opp180.text: Opposite angles across a crossing are equal. It's the neighbours that add to one eighty.
ln.hint.ang.opp180.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.adjEqual.text: These two angles are neighbours on a straight beam, so they add up to one eighty.
ln.hint.ang.adjEqual.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.vert360.text: Look at just one straight beam. The angles on it add up to half a turn.
ln.hint.ang.vert360.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.tri360.text: A triangle's angles make half a turn, not a full turn.
ln.hint.ang.tri360.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.isoHalf.text: What's left is shared by two equal angles. Split it in half.
ln.hint.ang.isoHalf.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.isoDouble.text: Remember the other base angle: it's the same size. Take both away.
ln.hint.ang.isoDouble.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.par180.text: Look at the letter shape. F and Z angles are equal, not adding to one eighty.
ln.hint.ang.par180.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.cointEqual.text: These make a C shape. Co-interior angles add up to one eighty.
ln.hint.ang.cointEqual.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.par360.text: Find the letter shape first: F, Z or C. A full turn isn't part of it.
ln.hint.ang.par360.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.noHalf.text: Nearly there. That's both equal angles together. Now share it between them.
ln.hint.ang.noHalf.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.oneStep.text: That's one step done. Now use the triangle to find the angle at the boat.
ln.hint.ang.oneStep.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ang.usedExterior.text: The outside angle isn't in the triangle. Find the inside angle at the buoy first.
ln.hint.ang.usedExterior.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.bear.marked.text: That's the marked angle. Bearings are measured from north, turning clockwise.
ln.hint.bear.marked.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.bear.wrongSide.text: Check which way the ship is from the compass point. Is it clockwise or anticlockwise?
ln.hint.bear.wrongSide.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.bear.anticlockwise.text: Bearings always turn clockwise from north, like the hands of a clock.
ln.hint.bear.anticlockwise.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.bear.same.text: That's the way the ship looks at us. We need to look back the other way.
ln.hint.bear.same.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.bear.mirror.text: The opposite direction is half a turn round, not a mirror image.
ln.hint.bear.mirror.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.bear.subtract.text: Turn half a turn from the ship's bearing: add or take away one eighty.
ln.hint.bear.subtract.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.pyth.added.text: Adding the sides doesn't work for slopes. Square them first.
ln.hint.pyth.added.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.pyth.noRoot.text: Good squaring. That number is the side squared, so take the square root.
ln.hint.pyth.noRoot.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.pyth.subtracted.text: Square the sides before you add or take away.
ln.hint.pyth.subtracted.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.pyth.usedHyp.text: The longest side is already given. Take away, don't add, before the square root.
ln.hint.pyth.usedHyp.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.pyth.truncate.text: Close! Look at the next digit. Five or more means round up.
ln.hint.pyth.truncate.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.pyth.wholeRound.text: Close! Keep one digit after the decimal point.
ln.hint.pyth.wholeRound.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.scale.divided.text: The real sea is much bigger than the chart, so the number should grow.
ln.hint.scale.divided.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.scale.multiplied.text: The chart is much smaller than the sea, so the number should shrink.
ln.hint.scale.multiplied.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.scale.added.text: A scale tells you how many times bigger, so multiply or divide, don't add.
ln.hint.scale.added.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.scale.noScale.text: That's the chart measurement. Now use the scale to turn it into real kilometres.
ln.hint.scale.noScale.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.share.onePart.text: That's one part. How many parts does this share get?
ln.hint.share.onePart.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.share.otherShare.text: That's the other share. Check which name the question asks about.
ln.hint.share.otherShare.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.share.equalSplit.text: A ratio share isn't half each. Count the parts in the ratio.
ln.hint.share.equalSplit.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.share.divByPart.text: Divide by all the parts together, not just one side of the ratio.
ln.hint.share.divByPart.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.swap.text: Those are swapped. Go across for x first, then up for y.
ln.hint.grid.swap.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.signX.text: Check the sign of x. Negative x goes left of the y-axis.
ln.hint.grid.signX.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.signY.text: Check the sign of y. Negative y goes down, below the x-axis.
ln.hint.grid.signY.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.runRise.text: Rise goes on top. How far up, divided by how far across.
ln.hint.grid.runRise.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.sign.text: Read from left to right. Does the path go uphill or downhill?
ln.hint.grid.sign.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.riseOnly.text: That's the rise. Now divide it by the run.
ln.hint.grid.riseOnly.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.intercept.text: That's where it crosses the y-axis. Gradient is how steep it is.
ln.hint.grid.intercept.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.xIcpt.text: That's where it crosses the x-axis. We need the y-axis, where x is zero.
ln.hint.grid.xIcpt.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.gradient.text: That's the gradient. The intercept is a point on the y-axis.
ln.hint.grid.gradient.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.grid.signC.text: Check whether it crosses above or below the x-axis.
ln.hint.grid.signC.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.kind.reflex.text: Follow the arc, not the gap. A sweep past a straight line is reflex.
ln.hint.kind.reflex.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.kind.right.text: Look for the little square. Only a right angle gets one.
ln.hint.kind.right.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.kind.size.text: Compare the sweep with a right angle, like the corner of a page.
ln.hint.kind.size.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.reason.vert.text: Vertically opposite angles share one crossing. These two are at different crossings.
ln.hint.reason.vert.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.reason.shape.text: Trace from one angle to the other along the lines. Is it an F, a Z or a C?
ln.hint.reason.shape.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.conv.add.text: Any triangle's two short sides add up to more. Square them to test for a right angle.
ln.hint.conv.add.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.conv.measure.text: We can tell from the sides alone. Pythagoras works backwards too.
ln.hint.conv.measure.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.conv.check.text: Work out both squares carefully, then compare them.
ln.hint.conv.check.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ratio.units.text: Centimetres and kilometres are different units. Make them match first.
ln.hint.ratio.units.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.ratio.zeros.text: Count the zeros. One kilometre is a hundred thousand centimetres.
ln.hint.ratio.zeros.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.eqn.swap.text: The number in front of x is the gradient. The number on its own is the intercept.
ln.hint.eqn.swap.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.eqn.sign.text: Uphill or downhill? That decides the sign of the gradient.
ln.hint.eqn.sign.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.eqn.inv.text: Check the steepness: rise over run, not run over rise.
ln.hint.eqn.inv.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.eqn.c.text: Check where the path crosses the y-axis.
ln.hint.eqn.c.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.meet.swap.text: Those coordinates are swapped. x comes first.
ln.hint.meet.swap.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.meet.icpt.text: That point is only on one path. The crossing must fit both.
ln.hint.meet.icpt.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.meet.sign.text: Check that point in both equations. Does it really fit?
ln.hint.meet.sign.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.para.sign.text: A minus gradient slopes the other way, so those paths do cross.
ln.hint.para.sign.speaker: ripple

ln.hint.para.samec.text: Starting at the same point isn't parallel. Compare the gradients.
ln.hint.para.samec.speaker: ripple

ln.praise.angle.text: You used the angle fact step by step.
ln.praise.angle.speaker: hoot

ln.praise.angle2.text: You found the fact that fits, then worked it out.
ln.praise.angle2.speaker: hoot

ln.praise.bearing.text: Clockwise from north, three figures. The beam is spot on.
ln.praise.bearing.speaker: hoot

ln.praise.pyth.text: You found the hypotenuse first and kept the working tidy.
ln.praise.pyth.speaker: hoot

ln.praise.scale.text: You used the scale carefully. The chart and the sea agree.
ln.praise.scale.speaker: hoot

ln.praise.share.text: You counted the parts first. That's the key to ratios.
ln.praise.share.speaker: hoot

ln.praise.graph.text: You read the graph carefully, across and up.
ln.praise.graph.speaker: hoot

ln.praise.home.text: You put two steps together. Bobbo is on his way home!
ln.praise.home.speaker: hoot

ln.retry.text: Not quite. Ripple has a tip.
ln.retry.speaker: hoot

ln.model.text: Here's how a keeper works it out. Follow each step, then confirm.
ln.model.speaker: ripple

ln.idle.text: Take your time. The ships will wait for a careful answer.
ln.idle.speaker: hoot
